title: About the ZSVR
content:
For the packaging recycling market to work effectively, financial interests have to be aligned. In other words, companies need to cover the costs of recycling their retail, grouped or shipment packaging. As the ZSVR, our task is to establish a level playing field and ensure that everybody is playing by the rules.

As a supervisory authority, our job is to create a level playing field and ensure costs are fairly distributed, with the ultimate aim of reducing the environmental impact of packaging waste and ensuring that packaging recycling costs are covered.

We operate the LUCID Packaging Register, which makes producer responsibility visible. We reconcile packaging volumes. And we publish standards promoting recycling-friendly packaging design.

We currently have 12 job openings.

Five landmark judgments in four months – each one confirms the ZSVR’s classification decisions and provides valuable practical guidance. Stay compliant by staying up to date.

The ZSVR's catalogue helps companies classify their products' packaging – and shows if it is subject to system participation, i.e. whether they have to pay for recycling or not.

Retail, shipment or transport packaging? Different legal obligations apply depending on packaging type. Understanding the differences helps people meet their packaging law obligations and avoid breaches, providing legal certainty and strengthening compliance.
